gaps.lead: He was sacked for constantly missing deadlines.
gaps.sentence: If he hadn't kept missing deadlines, he ___ sacked.
gaps.explanation: If + past perfect, would(n't) have been + participle.

gaps.lead: He couldn't swim until he was twenty.
gaps.sentence: He ___ swim until he was twenty.
gaps.explanation: couldn't = was not able to (general ability in the past).

gaps.lead: Fewer students enrolled this year than we expected.
gaps.explanation: fewer than expected = not as many (students) as expected.

gaps.lead: It wasn't necessary for her to bring any food — there was plenty.
gaps.explanation: needn't have + participle = it wasn't necessary, but she did it.

gaps.lead: The garage is servicing my car tomorrow morning.
gaps.explanation: Arranged service: have/get something done — having my car serviced.

gaps.lead: I always hated pasta when I was a child, but now I cook it regularly.
gaps.sentence: I ___ pasta when I was a child but now I cook it regularly.
gaps.explanation: 'used to + infinitive' describes a past state or habit that is no longer true.
